title: Greenfield: build a Go line-count CLI tool from scratch
description: Start with an empty Go module (go.mod only). Build a CLI that counts lines, words, and characters in one or more files (like wc). Include a proper package structure and tests.

injections.content:
# go-wc

A line/word/char counter CLI (like Unix `wc`).

Usage: `go-wc [--lines] [--words] [--chars] <file> [<file>...]`

Default (no flags): show all three counts.

task_spec.prompt:
Build a `wc`-like CLI tool from scratch in this Go module.

Structure:
  internal/counter/counter.go  — Count(r io.Reader) -> (lines, words, chars int, err error)
  internal/counter/counter_test.go  — at least 4 tests
  cmd/go-wc/main.go  — CLI: accepts one or more file paths, flags --lines/--words/--chars
    If no flags: print all three. If flag(s): print only requested counts.
    Format per file: <lines>\t<words>\t<chars>\t<filename>  (omit columns not requested)
    Exit 1 if any file fails to open.

Requirements:
- Use only stdlib (no external deps)
- counter.Count reads from io.Reader (testable without real files)
- 4+ tests in counter_test.go covering: empty input, single line, multi-line, unicode
- go test ./... must pass
- go build ./... must succeed
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
